Bug_Title: The "Object.finalize()" method should not be called
Bug_Details:
Before it reclaims storage from an object that is no longer referenced, the garbage collector calls finalize() on the object.
This is a good time to release resources held by the object.
Because the general contract is that the finalize method should only be called once per object, calling this method explicitly is
misleading and does not respect this contract.
What is the potential impact?
An explicit call to an object’s finalize method will perform operations that most likely were supposed to be performed only when the object was not
referenced anymore by any thread.
Since it is an acceptable practice to override the finalize method in any subclass of Object , by invoking it explicitly, we will run
code that was designed to only be ran at a different time.
Noncompliant code example
public void dispose() throws Throwable {
  this.finalize();                       // Noncompliant
}
Bug_Explanation: The code explicitly calls the finalize() method on an object, which is against the contract that finalize() should only be called by the garbage collector. This can lead to unexpected behavior since finalize() is intended to be called once an object is no longer in use, rather than manually during an object's lifecycle.
Trigger_Explanation: The JUnit test triggers the bug by explicitly calling the 'showBug()' method, which internally calls 'finalize()'. This is against the contract of the finalize method, which should only be invoked by the garbage collector, leading to the test failing.
